climate: Seasons this warm ripen Cabernet Sauvignon, Grenache, Carignan, Zinfandel and Nebbiolo fully without cooking off their freshness.
Tempranillo is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Syrah is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.

soil.rock: Sandstone is sand bound into rock. It weathers to light, sandy soil that drains freely.
soil.top: The topsoil drains fast and warms early in spring. Vines get little water, which keeps crops small and flavors concentrated, but drought bites hard. Its pH is close to neutral, so vines take up the nutrients they need easily.

land: The high ground runs about 3°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
Gentle slopes. Enough tilt to drain cold air and rain away, which lowers frost risk, yet still easy to farm by machine.

winkler: Big crops are possible, but quality tops out at acceptable.
